name: Shallum
summary:
Shallum of Israel was the fifteenth king of the ancient Kingdom of Israel, reigning for only one month in 752 BCE. He succeeded his brother Omri and was subsequently overthrown by his half-brother Jeroboam I.

Shallum's reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against neighboring territories, including the kingdom of Moab and the Ammonites. Despite these efforts, Shallum's rule was ultimately short-lived, as he was assassinated before he could solidify his hold on power.

The significance of Shallum's reign lies in its impact on the political landscape of ancient Israel. His brief but tumultuous rule sets the stage for the division of the kingdom and the subsequent rise of the House of David.

Shallum's legacy also extends to the cultural sphere, as his policies and actions influenced the development of the Hebrew Bible.

The reign of Shallum serves as a poignant reminder of the fragility of power in ancient Israel, where even brief periods of dominance could have far-reaching consequences.

The Assyrian Empire, which had long been a dominant force in the region, played a significant role in shaping Shallum's reign and its outcome. The empire's interests and ambitions had a profound impact on the politics and military campaigns of ancient Israel during this period.
